clue.text: Thriller has Maigret regularly chasing priest with revolver

indicators.note: the Maigret letters chase, or follow behind, the letter for priest
every other letter of Maigret is taken, at regular intervals

parts.note: the letters in positions two, four and six

explanation.surface: A crime thriller in which Simenon's detective pursues a gun-toting priest.
explanation.walkthrough: P is the standard abbreviation for priest. A revolver is read literally as anything that turns.
explanation.definitionFit: A page-turner is a gripping book, and a thriller is the classic example of one.

clue.text: Sailor's fishy oils hard to get rid of

indicators.note: something fishy is suspect or not right, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A seaman finds some suspect oils too hard to dispose of.
explanation.definitionFit: To abolish something is to do away with it entirely, a formal synonym.

clue.text: Central characters in Daniel Deronda are more mature

indicators.note: the answer sits in the middle of the novel's title, spanning its two words

parts.note: the last three letters of Daniel and first two of Deronda sit at the centre of the title

explanation.surface: The main characters in George Eliot's novel Daniel Deronda are grown-ups.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Central characters' suggests the novel's protagonists; here it means letters at the centre of the title.
explanation.definitionFit: Elder is the comparative of old, used for someone older or more senior.

clue.text: University degree received by blue-eyed boy's unaffordable to most people

indicators.note: the degree is taken inside the word for the favourite

parts.note: a mark on a scale, a level or grade

explanation.surface: A favoured student earns a university degree that ordinary people could never pay for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Degree' suggests a qualification like BA or MA, but here it is a point on a scale.
explanation.definitionFit: Upmarket goods are aimed at wealthy buyers, so they are too expensive for the mass market.

clue.text: Demand support for running trendy evening, not unknown to be a non-stop mission

indicators.note: in a down entry the demand sits beneath the rest, supporting it
in the sense of operating or working, telling us to rearrange the letters
the unknown is left out of the letters before they are rearranged

parts.note: y is one of the algebraic unknowns

explanation.surface: An organiser insists on help with a fashionable night out that seems to go on forever.
explanation.definitionFit: A never-ending task is a job that never finishes, a mission without a stopping point.

clue.text: Aagh! Wine brought round smelt disgusting

indicators.note: the wine is wrapped round the cry of alarm

explanation.surface: Someone shrieks because the wine served to them stank.
explanation.definitionFit: Reeked means gave off a strong, foul smell, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Examines key agreement

parts.note: yes is a word of assent

explanation.surface: Someone scrutinises the central terms of a deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key agreement' reads as a crucial deal, but each word works separately.
explanation.definitionFit: To eye something is to look it over, so eyes means examines or inspects.

clue.text: Rescue old fraud briefly put away

indicators.note: the last letter of the word for fraud is cut short

parts.note: to put away food is to eat it, so ate

explanation.surface: A former conman is locked up, and someone must save him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put away' suggests jailing the fraudster; it is the informal sense of eating a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: To extricate someone is to free them from a difficulty, which is to rescue them.

clue.text: Keen to make way without drug

indicators.note: the drug letter goes on the outside, ahead of the way

parts.note: to make money is to earn it

explanation.surface: An eager person clears a path while staying off drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnest means serious and eager, as in an earnest young student, close to keen.

clue.text: Courtyard at the back has trees

parts.note: Courtyard splits into court and yard; to court someone is to woo them

indicators.note: only the final letter of the second half of Courtyard is taken

explanation.surface: A rear courtyard has some trees in it.
explanation.walkthrough: The word Courtyard splits into its two parts, court and yard, which do separate jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: A wood is an area of land covered with growing trees.

clue.text: Initially Mary Astor perhaps struggles to be included with screen legends

indicators.note: only the opening letter of Mary is used
the struggles go inside the rearranged surname
perhaps suggests the letters may be some other order

explanation.surface: Mary Astor once had to fight to be counted among Hollywood's greats.
explanation.walkthrough: Mary Astor was a real Hollywood actress, which makes the surface feel like film history.
explanation.definitionFit: Movie stars are famous film actors, and the greatest of them are legends of the screen.

clue.text: Follow motorway slip heading off

parts.note: MI stands in for the M1, Britain's first motorway

indicators.note: the first letter of the slip is removed

explanation.surface: A driver is told to follow the slip road leaving the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the motorway from London to Leeds; the digit 1 is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: To mirror someone is to copy or imitate them, closely following what they do.

clue.text: Engineers computers, indeed malfunctioning, tweaked once more

parts.note: indeed splits as in plus deed: the computing letters IT go in a malfunctioning, jumbled deed

explanation.surface: Engineers find the computers really are faulty.
explanation.walkthrough: The word indeed splits into in and deed; RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps.
explanation.definitionFit: To re-edit a text is to revise it again, making further adjustments.

clue.text: This clue's next, comprising anagram of tree

definitions.text: This clue's next, comprising anagram of tree

parts.words: This clue's next, comprising anagram of tree
parts.note: this clue follows the twelfth across clue, so its answer is its own number, and that number word holds the four letters of tree jumbled

explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the number of the clue itself, which follows 12-across. THIRTEEN contains RTEE, a rearrangement of tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue is numbered as the integer after twelve, so its own label is the answer.

clue.text: Circuit's consuming a conservative half of carbon that's used in F1

indicators.note: consuming means the circuit swallows the letters that follow

parts.note: a ring is a circuit, as in a racing ring

indicators.note: half of keeps the first three of carbon's six letters

explanation.surface: A racetrack eats up a Tory and half the carbon burnt in Formula One.
explanation.walkthrough: F1 is Formula One motor racing.
explanation.definitionFit: A racing car is the vehicle driven in Formula One grand prix events.

clue.text: Not in favour of AI penning books

indicators.note: the AI encloses the books, as in a pen

explanation.surface: Someone objects to artificial intelligence writing books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penning' looks like writing, but it means enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: Anti as a preposition means opposed to, against.

clue.text: Reproduced brave review of US college word for word

indicators.note: made again in a different form, so the letters are rearranged
read in reverse, a re-view backwards

parts.note: MIT, the Massachusetts Institute of Technology

explanation.surface: A bold review of an American university has been reprinted exactly.
explanation.definitionFit: Verbatim means in exactly the same words as the original, an exact repetition.

clue.text: Design with pronounced flaw

indicators.note: said out loud, the word for a flaw gives the answer

parts.note: a speck is a tiny mark or blemish

explanation.surface: A design with an obvious defect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pronounced' looks like conspicuous, describing the flaw, but it signals a word said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: A spec, short for specification, is a detailed design or plan.

clue.text: Paltry amount of snacks

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the nuts eaten as a snack

explanation.walkthrough: 'Paltry amount of snacks' reads as a stingy portion; the two parts are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both slang for a tiny payment and the plural of a legume nut.

clue.text: Chief Engineer's to live among mobile rigs which float in cold seas

indicators.note: the engineer and the living go in among the scrambled letters
movable, so the letters shift around

explanation.surface: An engineer will live on moving oil rigs in the freezing ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Icebergs are huge masses of floating ice found in polar waters.

clue.text: Weapon's prepared off 'en garde!'

indicators.note: made ready from the phrase, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fencer's sword is readied after the call to take guard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'En garde' is the fencer's warning to get on guard.
explanation.definitionFit: A grenade is a small bomb thrown by hand, an explosive weapon.

clue.text: Allow new girl, ignoring the odds, to mount beam

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up the column means the letters are read upwards
only the second and fourth letters of girl are kept

explanation.surface: Someone lets a new girl climb a gym beam despite the risk.
explanation.definitionFit: A lintel is a horizontal beam over a door or window.

clue.text: Jack's good squeezing relative in and going for a spin

indicators.note: the jack and good letters press around the relative

parts.note: J in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: Jack kindly squeezes a family member into the car for a drive.
explanation.definitionFit: Jaunting is taking a short pleasure trip, as on an Irish jaunting car.

clue.text: Brother has adopted lounge jacket

indicators.note: the brother takes the lounge into the family, inside it

parts.note: to laze is to lounge about

explanation.surface: A sibling has taken to wearing a lounge jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lounge jacket' looks like one item, but lounge is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: A blazer is a smart jacket, often in club or school colours.

clue.text: Addiction support group's welcoming girl in one more time

indicators.note: the group takes the girl into its midst

parts.note: G is a dictionary abbreviation for girl

explanation.surface: An addiction group welcomes a woman back for another session.
explanation.definitionFit: Again means once more, a repetition of something.

clue.text: Shrewd diplomacy admitting nothing decisive

indicators.note: letting nothing in, so the zero goes inside

explanation.surface: Shrewd diplomacy that lets nothing in is a decisive force.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone quick to act responds without hesitation, which is to be decisive.

clue.text: Armistice for aggressive Russian leaders is a long way away

indicators.note: the first letters of the four words lead them

parts.note: the opening letter of each of these four words

explanation.surface: A ceasefire for warlike Russian rulers is still distant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaders' suggests Kremlin rulers; it points to initial letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Afar means at a great distance, a poetic word for far off.

clue.text: Employer requires uniform, on contracts ending, to be returned

indicators.note: the whole string is sent back the other way

parts.note: re, regarding; the same letters also lie reversed across requires uniform, a happy coincidence of the surface

indicators.note: only the last letter of contracts

explanation.surface: A boss demands staff hand back uniforms when their contracts end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Employer' suggests a boss; here it means one who employs or uses something.
explanation.definitionFit: A user is anyone who makes use of something, one who employs it.

clue.text: Of the same opinion as journalist about intelligence

indicators.note: the journalist is attached around the end of the intelligence

parts.note: like, in the sense of similar to

explanation.surface: Someone agrees with a reporter on matters of intelligence.
explanation.definitionFit: Like-minded people share the same views and outlook, so they agree.
